description.value: This study examined whether baseline static and dynamic resting-state network properties of the rTMS target predict changes in emotion-regulation distress in patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder.

spans.text: The current study aims to expound the application of (dynamic) network analysis to predict response to excitatory dlPFC-rTMS on distress ratings during an emotional task paradigm

value: We hypothesize that baseline network properties of the rTMS target may help understand this variation and predict response.

Participants with greater baseline local, segregated, connectivity of the target node and/or subnetwork are expected to show a greater behavioral change after excitatory rTMS compared to participants with more integratively connected target regions.

spans.text: We hypothesize that individual response is predicted by baseline (dynamic) resting-state network topology of the target region and its associated subnetwork of connected brain regions.

description.value: Participants underwent three measurements over 1–4 weeks; OCD patients received excitatory dlPFC rTMS or active-control vertex stimulation, while healthy controls received inhibitory dlPFC rTMS or active-control vertex stimulation.

description.value: Resting-state fMRI preprocessing including brain extraction, tissue segmentation, registration, discarding the first four volumes, motion correction, spatial smoothing, high-pass filtering, nuisance regression, region exclusion, and scrubbing.

spans.text: The rsfMRI preprocessing steps included: (a) extraction of brain tissue using BET [ ] and tissue type segmentation using FAST on participants’ native structural scan [ ], (b) coregistration of rsfMRI to the structural scan using FLIRT and FNIRT in order to warp atlas regions to individual functional images, (c) application of several preprocessing steps through MELODIC [ ], namely discarding the first 4 vol, motion correction using McFLIRT [ ], spatial smoothing at 5 mm full width half maximum using SUSAN [ ], and a high pass filter of 100 s cut-off, (d) regression of time series from voxels in the white matter and cerebrospinal fluid, (e) exclusion of atlas regions containing <4 active voxels in any participant, which yielded a total of 200 regions common to all datasets.
Most imaging analysis was performed using FMRIB’s software library (FSL 5.0.10 [ ]).
